title: The constructive number-theory grand campaign
subtitle: 120 major first-order arithmetic milestones, sixteen foundations, and eight honestly classified existing proof anchors

dependency_policy.deps: Actual construction prerequisites only; every dependency arrow advances strictly to a later campaign layer.
dependency_policy.conceptual_refs: Optional mathematical connections that are not proof prerequisites, do not create arrows, do not block scheduling, and confer no evidence authority.

language.logic: Intuitionistic first-order Heyting arithmetic with its ordinary induction schema; all quantified variables denote natural-number codes.
language.conservative_extension_policy: Every named relation below abbreviates an arithmetical formula over the base signature. Integers, rationals, finite lists, sets, polynomials, finite fields, matrices, lattices, curves, algorithms, and certificates are explicit natural-number codes. No new sort, axiom, excluded middle, infinitary choice, or oracle is admitted.
language.notation_policy: Order, signed arithmetic, exponentiation, division, factorials, bounded sums and products, finite set notation, logarithm brackets, and rational inequalities expand into witnessed first-order primitive-recursive relations.
language.finite_objects: Gödel beta codes represent finite lists, tables, machines, traces, finite-precision local data, and certificates; every bounded quantifier expands in first-order arithmetic.

Even.meaning: A witnessed exact even natural, shared with the historical checked parity definition.

Odd.meaning: A witnessed exact odd natural, shared with the historical checked parity definition.

Mod.expansion: m>0 ∧ a,b have the same witnessed remainder modulo m

ModEq.meaning: Balanced witnessed congruence for any natural modulus, including the exact-equality zero-modulus case.

Gcd.expansion: Dvd(g,a) ∧ Dvd(g,b) ∧ ∀ d. Dvd(d,a) ∧ Dvd(d,b) → Dvd(d,g)

Mod4Three.meaning: The exact witnessed residue class three modulo four.

PrimeThreeModFourDivisor.meaning: A genuine prime divisor in the exact residue class three modulo four.

EuclidThreeNumber.meaning: The subtraction-free Euclidean witness 4*(c-1)+3 in the exact residue class three modulo four.

BertrandWindow.meaning: An exact strict prime witness in Bertrand's open interval.

AllBits.meaning: A complete beta-coded finite prefix containing only binary digits.

BitCount.meaning: The exact witnessed number of one bits in a complete beta-coded digit prefix.
BitCount.expansion: AllBits(b,c,l) ∧ z is the witnessed sum of the complete beta-coded bit prefix

BertrandChain.meaning: A beta-coded finite chain beginning at n with a strict Bertrand prime step at every bounded edge.
BertrandChain.expansion: Beta(b,c,0,n) ∧ ∀i. Lt(i,k) → ∃u v. Beta(b,c,i,u) ∧ Beta(b,c,i+1,v) ∧ BertrandWindow(u,v)

Seq.meaning: A beta-coded list of length ell.
Seq.expansion: s encodes beta parameters and the witnessed natural length ell

At.expansion: i is below the coded length of s and its beta-extracted value equals x

Sum.expansion: a coded partial-sum trace starts at zero and ends at z

BetaSum.meaning: The exact four-argument checked beta-prefix sum, kept distinct from the three-argument generic research-planning Sum relation.
BetaSum.expansion: ∃u v. Beta(u,v,0,0) ∧ Beta(u,v,l,z) ∧ ∀i. Lt(i,l) → ∃a x y. Beta(b,c,i,a) ∧ Beta(u,v,i,x) ∧ Beta(u,v,S(i),y) ∧ y=x+a

Prod.expansion: a coded partial-product trace starts at one and ends at z

Pow.expansion: a length e+1 multiplication trace starts at one and ends at z

Fact.expansion: z is the coded finite product of 1 through n

Val.meaning: p-adic valuation only for a positive natural.

PowerValuation.meaning: Conservative named alias for the exact positive-input prime-power valuation.

PowerValuationOne.meaning: Exact prime-power valuation one, including the supplied positive-input witness.

FactorialValuation.meaning: A supplied witnessed valuation of the witnessed factorial.

LegendreSum.meaning: The witnessed finite prime-power quotient sum.
LegendreSum.expansion: a beta-coded quotient prefix lists floor(n/p), floor(n/p²), … through the explicit bounded cutoff and its witnessed sum is e

Binom.expansion: z is obtained from the witnessed finite Pascal recurrence, with out-of-range values zero

Multinom.expansion: parts is a finite nonnegative list summing to n and z is its iterated binomial product

Digits.expansion: p>1 and the coded digits are below p and evaluate to n

CarryCount.expansion: a witnessed columnwise addition of the coded parts contains exactly e carries

Factorization.expansion: n>0, every list entry is Prime, and the witnessed product is n

Permutation.meaning: Witnessed equality up to finite permutation.
Permutation.expansion: w is a coded bijection matching all list entries

PrimeList.expansion: s lists exactly k increasing primes and omits no smaller prime

DivisorList.expansion: n>0 and s lists exactly the positive divisors d≤n

Phi.expansion: n>0 and t counts the residue classes a<n satisfying Coprime(a,n)

Jordan.expansion: k>0,n>0 and t counts the coded k-tuples modulo n jointly coprime to n

Mobius.expansion: z is zero for a squared prime divisor and otherwise the signed parity of distinct prime factors

ArithmeticTable.expansion: f is a beta-coded signed-value table on the positive naturals ≤N

Convolution.meaning: Finite signed Dirichlet convolution on positive inputs.
Convolution.expansion: for each n satisfying 0<n≤N, the table h(n) is the signed finite sum of f(d)*g(n/d) over positive divisors d

Squarefree.expansion: n>0 and no PRIME p≤n satisfies Dvd(p*p,n)

PowerProfile.meaning: Finite perfect-power certificate with the unit exception.
PowerProfile.expansion: (n=1 and w certifies the uniform identity ∀k>0.1=1^k) OR (n>1 and w lists the finitely many PRIME valuations, their positive gcd, and the witnessed roots for its positive divisors)

Order.expansion: a is a unit in the coded finite group, a^d=1, and no smaller positive exponent does

CRTCompatible.expansion: every positive listed modulus pair has gcd dividing its signed residue difference

CRTSolution.expansion: M is the lcm of all positive listed moduli, x<M, and every listed congruence holds

CRTPositiveModuliPrefix.meaning: Every actual entry of a beta-coded finite modulus prefix is positive.

CRTPairwiseCoprimePrefix.meaning: All distinct positions of a beta-coded finite modulus prefix contain coprime entries.
CRTPairwiseCoprimePrefix.expansion: ∀i j m n. Lt(i,l) → Lt(j,l) → ¬(i=j) → Beta(b,c,i,m) → Beta(b,c,j,n) → Coprime(m,n)

CRTPrefixSolution.meaning: A simultaneous solution at every actually decoded finite-list residue and modulus position, including the zero-modulus equality case.
CRTPrefixSolution.expansion: ∀i a m. Lt(i,l) → Beta(r,s,i,a) → Beta(b,c,i,m) → ∃q h. x+m*q=a+m*h

CRTPrefixLCM.meaning: The universal-property least common multiple of every actually decoded finite-list modulus, including arbitrary non-coprime and zero entries.
CRTPrefixLCM.expansion: (∀i m. Lt(i,l) → Beta(b,c,i,m) → Dvd(m,M)) ∧ (∀N. (∀i m. Lt(i,l) → Beta(b,c,i,m) → Dvd(m,N)) → Dvd(M,N))

CRTCanonicalPrefixSolution.meaning: An exact simultaneous finite-list solution strictly bounded by its genuine universal-property list LCM.

CRTPairwiseCompatiblePrefix.meaning: Every actual pair of beta-coded residues is congruent modulo the relational gcd of its actual possibly non-coprime or zero moduli.
CRTPairwiseCompatiblePrefix.expansion: ∀i j a d m n g. Lt(i,l) → Lt(j,l) → Beta(r,s,i,a) → Beta(r,s,j,d) → Beta(b,c,i,m) → Beta(b,c,j,n) → Gcd(m,n,g) → ModEq(g,a,d)

CRTMergeCompatiblePrefix.meaning: Every next actual congruence is compatible with every actual predecessor solution modulo the gcd of its modulus and the universal-property predecessor LCM.
CRTMergeCompatiblePrefix.expansion: ∀i x M a n g. Lt(i,l) → CRTPrefixLCM(b,c,i,M) → CRTPrefixSolution(r,s,b,c,i,x) → Beta(r,s,i,a) → Beta(b,c,i,n) → Gcd(M,n,g) → ModEq(g,x,a)

Carmichael.expansion: m>1,c>0, every unit has cth power one, and no smaller positive exponent works

PrimitiveRootModulus.meaning: Exact modulus classification with primitive roots.
PrimitiveRootModulus.expansion: w witnesses m=2, m=4, m=p^k, or m=2*p^k for an odd Prime p and k>0

PrimeCount.expansion: z counts the explicitly bounded list of primes p≤x

BinaryDigit.meaning: A witnessed unique quotient and zero-or-one binary digit.

BitLen.meaning: The unique witnessed binary length, with zero represented by one binary digit.
BitLen.expansion: (n=0 ∧ ell=1) ∨ (n>0 ∧ ∃e lower upper. ell=e+1 ∧ PowTwo(e,lower) ∧ PowTwo(ell,upper) ∧ lower≤n ∧ n<upper)

LogBracket.meaning: Certified rational lower and upper bounds on log x.
LogBracket.expansion: x>0, L and U are signed rational codes, and w is a finite rational-series reduction and explicit remainder certificate witnessing L≤log(x)≤U

GaussBit.expansion: Prime(p),p>2,p∤a and s is the parity of the finite least-residue negative-representative count

JacobiBit.expansion: n is positive and odd, Coprime(a,n), and s is the factorwise quadratic-bit sum modulo two

HilbertBit.expansion: a,b are nonzero rational codes and s is computed by the explicit real, dyadic, or odd-PRIME local formula

HilbertProduct.meaning: Complete canonical verified finite rational Hilbert support.
HilbertProduct.expansion: w is the canonical DUPLICATE-FREE list containing EXACTLY ONCE the real place, the dyadic prime 2, and EVERY prime dividing any numerator or denominator of nonzero rationals a,b; for EACH listed place v it also supplies and verifies the actual local value HilbertBit(a,b,v,s_v)

Gaussian.expansion: z codes normalized signed integers a,b representing a+b*i

GNorm.expansion: z=(a,b) and n=a²+b² in signed-code arithmetic

Eisenstein.expansion: z codes normalized signed integers a,b representing a+b*omega

ENorm.expansion: z=(a,b) and n=a²-a*b+b² in signed-code arithmetic

Primary.expansion: z is coprime to the ramified prime and satisfies the witnessed finite primary residue convention

RingPrime.meaning: Prime element in a coded Euclidean ring.
RingPrime.expansion: z is a nonzero nonunit and every norm-bounded factorization has a unit factor

PowerSymbol.expansion: pi is an admissible prime, a is coprime to pi, and the finite residue-field power equals the ellth root indexed by s

PowerReciprocity.meaning: Higher reciprocity with all correction factors.
PowerReciprocity.expansion: w lists every finite ramified and infinite-place correction and verifies the resulting power-symbol product identity

FiniteSet.expansion: A codes exactly k distinct members of the specified finite ambient space

SetSum.expansion: S lists all and only distinct sums a+b in the specified coded ambient group

RestrictedSum.expansion: S lists all and only a+b with distinct entries a≠b of A

ZeroSubsequence.meaning: Zero-sum subsequence of distinct INDEX positions.
ZeroSubsequence.expansion: w chooses k distinct list indices, allowing repeated element values, whose sum in G is zero

ArithmeticProgression.expansion: d≠0 in the ambient group and every element of A equals a+i*d for a witnessed i<ell

CapSet.expansion: A has k distinct coded vectors and contains no three distinct vectors with coordinatewise zero sum modulo three

Poly.expansion: f is a coded list of degree at most d in the specified arithmetically presented ring

Horner.meaning: An exact beta-coded natural-polynomial evaluation trace.
Horner.expansion: ∃u v. Beta(u,v,0,0) ∧ Beta(u,v,ell,z) ∧ ∀i. Lt(i,ell) → ∃a r s. Beta(b,c,i,a) ∧ Beta(u,v,i,r) ∧ Beta(u,v,i+1,s) ∧ s=r*x+a

HornerDerivativeTrace.meaning: A pair of coupled beta-coded Horner traces computing both a natural polynomial and its exact formal derivative.
HornerDerivativeTrace.expansion: Beta(u,v,0,0) ∧ Beta(d,e,0,0) ∧ ∀i. Lt(i,l) → ∃a q q1 h h1. Beta(b,c,i,a) ∧ Beta(u,v,i,q) ∧ Beta(u,v,i+1,q1) ∧ Beta(d,e,i,h) ∧ Beta(d,e,i+1,h1) ∧ q1=q*t+a ∧ h1=h*t+q

HornerDerivative.meaning: The simultaneous final value and exact formal derivative of a beta-coded finite natural polynomial.
HornerDerivative.expansion: ∃u v d e. HornerDerivativeTrace(b,c,t,l,u,v,d,e) ∧ Beta(u,v,l,n) ∧ Beta(d,e,l,z) ∧ Horner(b,c,t,l,n)

HornerDerivativeOnly.meaning: The exact formal derivative of a beta-coded finite natural polynomial at the supplied evaluation point.

HornerTaylorRemainder.meaning: An exact witnessed subtraction-free quadratic Taylor remainder for a beta-coded natural polynomial, its checked formal derivative, and a shifted evaluation.

HenselCorrection.meaning: A canonical bounded correction digit making the derivative-weighted residual vanish modulo its actual modulus.

Eval.expansion: a finite witnessed Horner trace over R evaluates f(x)=y

Irred.meaning: Monic irreducibility over a PRIME field.
Irred.expansion: Prime(p), deg(f)>0, f monic, and every degree-bounded factorization modulo p has a constant factor

FiniteField.expansion: Prime(p), k>0, and F encodes an irreducible degree-k polynomial and all quotient-ring arithmetic tables

PolyFactorization.expansion: f≠0 and w lists a unit, all monic irreducible factors, and every positive multiplicity

SquarefreeDecomposition.expansion: f≠0 and w handles derivative-zero inseparable parts via explicit characteristic-p root extraction

RepCount.meaning: Number of ORDERED SIGNED r-square representations.
RepCount.expansion: k counts signed tuples in the explicit finite box [-n,n]^r of square sum n

MatrixAt.meaning: A flattened beta-coded finite matrix cell.

MatrixSkipIndex.meaning: The exact order-preserving original coordinate obtained by skipping one arbitrary deleted matrix row or column.

MatrixMinorCell.meaning: The exact beta-coded matrix cell surviving deletion of arbitrary designated row and column indices.

MatrixMinorPrefix.meaning: A complete row-major beta-coded finite prefix of an arbitrary-dimensional cofactor minor.
MatrixMinorPrefix.expansion: ∀k. Lt(k,l) → ∃i j z. k=q*i+j ∧ Lt(j,q) ∧ MatrixMinorCell(b,c,w,r,d,i,j,z) ∧ Beta(u,v,k,z)

SignedMatrixMinor.meaning: An exact arbitrary-dimensional signed matrix minor with independently coded positive and negative components.

MatrixMinorFourCode.meaning: The exact nested doubled-Cantor code of the four actual beta parameters describing one signed matrix minor.

SignedMinorRecord.meaning: An injectively packed record of the genuine signed q-by-q minor obtained by deleting the first row and exact column j.

SignedCofactorMinorPrefix.meaning: A complete beta-coded finite prefix of exact injectively packed first-row signed cofactor minors.

SignedAlternatingCofactorTerm.meaning: The exact subtraction-free positive and negative components of the signed product multiplied by the parity sign (-1)^i.

SignedAlternatingProductPrefix.meaning: Two complete beta-coded output streams containing every actual parity-correct signed cofactor-product component.
SignedAlternatingProductPrefix.expansion: ∀i ap an bp bn p n. Lt(i,l) → Beta(ab,ac,i,ap) → Beta(db,dc,i,an) → Beta(eb,ec,i,bp) → Beta(fb,fc,i,bn) → Beta(ub,uc,i,p) → Beta(vb,vc,i,n) → SignedAlternatingCofactorTerm(ap,an,bp,bn,i,p,n)

SignedAlternatingCofactorFold.meaning: The exact arbitrary-length subtraction-free positive/negative sum of every parity-correct signed cofactor product.

SignedFirstRowCofactorFold.meaning: An exact arbitrary-dimensional signed alternating cofactor fold using the actual decoded positive and negative first row of the input matrix.

DotProduct.meaning: The exact finite sum of pointwise products of two beta-coded natural vectors.
DotProduct.expansion: ∃u v k q. Beta(k,q,0,0) ∧ Beta(k,q,ell,z) ∧ ∀i. Lt(i,ell) → ∃a s t r w. Beta(b,c,i,a) ∧ Beta(d,e,i,s) ∧ Beta(u,v,i,t) ∧ t=a*s ∧ Beta(k,q,i,r) ∧ Beta(k,q,i+1,w) ∧ w=r+t

SignedDet2.meaning: The exact positive and negative natural components of a signed two-by-two determinant.

MatrixAffineSlice.meaning: A complete beta-coded finite affine reindexing of a matrix row or column.

MatrixProductCell.meaning: One exact natural matrix-product entry obtained from an independently coded row and column.
MatrixProductCell.expansion: ∃ub uc vb vc. MatrixAffineSlice(lb,lc,i*w,1,ub,uc,w) ∧ MatrixAffineSlice(rb,rc,j,v,vb,vc,w) ∧ DotProduct(ub,uc,vb,vc,w,n)

MatrixProductPrefix.meaning: A complete row-major beta-coded finite prefix of an arbitrary natural matrix product.
MatrixProductPrefix.expansion: ∀k. Lt(k,l) → ∃i j n. k=i*v+j ∧ Lt(j,v) ∧ MatrixProductCell(lb,lc,rb,rc,w,v,i,j,n) ∧ Beta(tb,tc,k,n)

MatrixPointwiseAdd.meaning: A beta-coded finite pointwise natural sum used to combine signed matrix-product components.
MatrixPointwiseAdd.expansion: ∀i. Lt(i,l) → ∃x y z. Beta(mb,mc,i,x) ∧ Beta(sb,sc,i,y) ∧ Beta(tb,tc,i,z) ∧ z=x+y

SignedDotProduct.meaning: The exact positive and negative dot-product components of two arbitrary finite signed vectors.
SignedDotProduct.expansion: ∃pp nn pn np. DotProduct(ab,ac,eb,ec,l,pp) ∧ DotProduct(db,dc,fb,fc,l,nn) ∧ DotProduct(ab,ac,fb,fc,l,pn) ∧ DotProduct(db,dc,eb,ec,l,np) ∧ p=pp+nn ∧ n=pn+np

SignedMatrixProduct.meaning: A full arbitrary-dimensional signed matrix product with independently beta-coded positive and negative output matrices.
SignedMatrixProduct.expansion: four witnessed MatrixProductPrefix computations are combined by two MatrixPointwiseAdd codes across all r*v output entries, including zero-width boundaries

IntMatrix.expansion: M is a beta-coded r-by-c table of signed integer codes

PositiveDefinite.expansion: w supplies strictly positive leading principal minors of a symmetric rational Gram matrix

QuadForm.expansion: x is an integer vector of length r and x-transpose*Q*x=n in signed-code arithmetic

ThreeSquareClass.meaning: A primitive positive nondegenerate ternary form equivalent to three squares.
ThreeSquareClass.expansion: U is an explicitly unimodular integer 3-by-3 matrix and Q=U-transpose*I3*U

LocalRepresentation.meaning: Complete relevant real, dyadic, and integral local certificates.
LocalRepresentation.expansion: n>0 and w checks positivity, the dyadic 4^a*(8b+7) obstruction, and every relevant discriminant-prime integral condition

ClassicallyIntegral.expansion: Q is a symmetric integral Gram matrix representing integers on all coded integer vectors

ListCell.meaning: The exact tagged natural-number list cell storing a Euclidean quotient and coded tail.
ListCell.expansion: s is the witnessed conservative natural pair-cell code of quotient q and tail t

ContinuedFractionTrace.meaning: A finite beta-coded reverse Euclidean history and its forward quotient list.
ContinuedFractionTrace.expansion: Beta codes every witnessed Lt-descending Euclidean division state and ListCell links its complete quotient list s through exactly ell transitions

ContinuedFraction.expansion: a,b>0 and s is the complete witnessed Euclidean quotient list for a/b

EuclideanDivision.meaning: An exact positive-divisor Euclidean division transition.

EuclideanHalving.meaning: The strict two-step Euclidean descent inequality.

EuclideanExecution.meaning: A complete beta-coded Euclidean history together with an independently certified relational gcd; terminal-state identification is not asserted.

EuclideanCommonDivisor.meaning: A genuine witnessed common divisor of two Euclidean states.

EuclideanStateAt.meaning: The uniquely decodable packed beta state at a Euclidean history index.

EuclideanAnchoredExecution.meaning: A complete actual Euclidean history whose terminal zero-remainder state is exactly its certified gcd output.

EuclideanBoundedTrace.meaning: An actual complete beta-coded Euclidean trace with a witnessed upper bound on its transition count.

EuclideanLogarithmicExecution.meaning: A terminal-state-identified Euclidean gcd execution bounded by twice the exact binary length plus one.

BinaryModulus.meaning: The positive nontrivial modulus required by binary modular exponentiation.

BinaryExponentSplit.meaning: An exact binary parity decomposition of a natural exponent.

CanonicalModularResidue.meaning: The uniquely bounded canonical residue of a natural modulo a positive modulus.

BinaryDoubledPower.meaning: The exact even-exponent repeated-squaring power transition.

BinaryOddPower.meaning: The exact odd-exponent square-and-multiply power transition.

BinaryModularStep.meaning: One exact bounded modular square or square-and-multiply transition.

BinaryModularPower.meaning: The unique canonical modular residue of the witnessed natural power a to exponent e.

BinaryDigitPrefix.meaning: A complete witnessed beta-coded finite sequence of zero-or-one digits.

BinaryExecutionTrace.meaning: A real beta-coded repeated-squaring accumulator history.
BinaryExecutionTrace.expansion: Beta(h,t,0,1) ∧ ∀i. Lt(i,n) → ∃b u v. Beta(d,s,i,b) ∧ Beta(h,t,i,u) ∧ Beta(h,t,i+1,v) ∧ BinaryModularStep(m,u,a,b,v)

BinaryModularExecution.meaning: A complete witnessed square-and-multiply execution together with its actual terminal result.

BinaryExecutionPowerInvariant.meaning: The exact base-two Horner value of a coded digit prefix and its canonical modular power.

BinaryExponentDigitCode.meaning: A complete beta-coded binary digit prefix evaluating exactly to the supplied exponent.

BinaryCanonicalExponentDigitCode.meaning: A binary exponent digit code whose length is the exact canonical BitLen witness.

BinaryCompleteModularExecution.meaning: A complete square-and-multiply execution for the canonical digits of an arbitrary exponent with its exact bounded modular-power output.

BinaryExecutionOperationCount.meaning: The exact actual operation count of the canonical binary execution, including the witnessed number of one digits.

Convergent.expansion: u,v>0 are obtained by the explicit two-term numerator and denominator recurrences

QuadraticPeriod.expansion: D>0 is nonsquare and s witnesses repetition of a complete-quotient state with least positive period ell

PrimitiveTriple.meaning: A positive primitive ordered Pythagorean triple in either leg orientation.

Cyclotomic.expansion: m>0, f is monic and integral, and the witnessed product over d dividing m equals X^m-1

RegularPrime.expansion: p is an odd PRIME and w checks p divides no numerator of B2,B4,…,B(p-3) via finite rational computations

SimpleLift.expansion: Prime(p),k>0,f(a)=0 modulo p^k,f′(a) is a unit modulo p, b=a modulo p^k, and f(b)=0 modulo p^(k+1)

AllRootLifts.meaning: The exact possibly empty list of one-step root lifts.
AllRootLifts.expansion: Prime(p),k>0 and S lists precisely the t

WeierstrassCertificate.meaning: Normalized preparation from sufficient COUPLED finite source precision.
WeierstrassCertificate.expansion: Prime(p),k>0,0<d<M, f is a distinguished HA-total coefficient-function code with a supplied precision modulus, and w verifies the canonical complete-ring factorization through the requested output precision; no uniqueness is inferred from naive independent truncations

PrattCertificate.expansion: c is a finite tree proving the factorization of n-1 and a witnessed primitive root

PocklingtonCertificate.expansion: c proves a factor F of n-1 with F>sqrt(n) and supplies all modular-power and gcd checks

EllipticCertificate.expansion: c supplies nonsingular curve checks, a certified large prime order factor, suitable point witnesses, and recursive smaller-prime certificates

Curve.expansion: E is a finite coefficient code and its discriminant is a witnessed unit of the declared field F

ECPoint.expansion: P is the distinguished infinity code or a normalized projective solution of the homogeneous curve equation

ECAdd.expansion: R is computed by the appropriate witnessed infinity, inverse, doubling, or distinct-point chord formula

ECCount.meaning: Point count over a finite extension.
ECCount.expansion: Prime(p),r>0,Curve(E,Fp), and N counts every affine point over F_(p^r) plus infinity

WeilPairing.expansion: ell is PRIME and distinct from the field characteristic, F contains all ell-torsion and ellth roots, and a witnessed finite Miller trace evaluates z

Lattice.expansion: d>0,B is a d-by-d signed integral matrix, and D=|det(B)|>0

LLLReduced.expansion: U is unimodular, 1/4<delta<1, and B*U satisfies witnessed size-reduction and Lovász inequalities

SymmetricPolytope.expansion: C=-C about zero, C is bounded convex and d-dimensional, and a finite rational triangulation witnesses volume V

TwoDescent.meaning: A witnessed finite rational elliptic 2-descent for full rational 2-torsion.
TwoDescent.expansion: E has three witnessed distinct rational roots and w supplies finite two-coverings, a checked rational square-class descent map, real and dyadic tests, and finite support at discriminant and coefficient-denominator primes

SelmerWitness.meaning: A finite computable two-Selmer superset for full rational 2-torsion.
SelmerWitness.expansion: E has three witnessed distinct rational roots and S is a finite explicitly computed rational S-unit square-class Selmer group with complete real, dyadic, discriminant-prime, and denominator-prime local conditions

WeakMW.meaning: Restricted weak Mordell–Weil finiteness by finite Selmer injection.

nodes.why: Ordinary first-order induction is ambient HA, not a new reflection principle.

nodes.title: Decidable natural equality
nodes.statement: ∀ a b. a=b ∨ a≠b.
nodes.why: Equality of naturals is decidable intuitionistically without general excluded middle.

nodes.title: Witnessed natural order
nodes.statement: ∀ a b. a≤b ↔ ∃t. a+t=b.
nodes.why: Every comparison carries a first-order arithmetic witness.

nodes.title: Gödel beta coding
nodes.statement: ∀ ell,s. Seq(s,ell) → ∃b,c. ∀i<ell ∃x. Beta(b,c,i,x) ∧ At(s,i,x).
nodes.why: Lists and finite structures remain natural-number codes in one-sorted HA.

nodes.title: Bounded decidable search
nodes.statement: For each decidable arithmetic P: (∃n≤B.P(n)) → ∃n≤B. P(n) ∧ ∀j<n.¬P(j).
nodes.why: Finite minimization extracts a least witness without unbounded choice.

nodes.title: Euclidean division
nodes.statement: ∀ n d. d>0 → ∃q r. DivRem(n,d,q,r).
nodes.why: All quotient and residue computations start from explicitly witnessed division.

nodes.title: Bézout identity and gcd
nodes.statement: ∀ a b. a+b>0 → ∃g u v. Gcd(a,b,g) ∧ u*a+v*b=g in signed codes.
nodes.why: Canonical gcd and signed Bézout coefficients feed inverses and factorization.

nodes.title: Prime divisor extraction
nodes.statement: ∀ n>1. ∃p q. Prime(p) ∧ n=p*q.
nodes.why: A nontrivial natural has a bounded explicitly extracted prime divisor.

nodes.title: Bounded p-adic valuation
nodes.statement: ∀ p n. Prime(p) ∧ n>0 → ∃e u. n=p^e*u ∧ ¬Dvd(p,u).
nodes.why: The complete independently checked Alpha-v19 residual closure promotes both exact prime-specific existence/functionality wrappers; together with the previously closed cofactor and multiplicativity theorems, all four members of this exact prime-valuation interface now have checked use.

nodes.title: Constructive Chinese remaindering
nodes.statement: ∀ a b m n. m,n>0 ∧ Coprime(m,n) → ∃x<m*n. Mod(x,a,m) ∧ Mod(x,b,n).
nodes.why: Coprime congruences compose using actual Bézout and inverse witnesses.

nodes.title: Finite sums and products
nodes.statement: ∀ s ell. Seq(s,ell) → ∃u v. Sum(s,ell,u) ∧ Prod(s,ell,v).
nodes.why: Every bounded aggregate has a checkable recurrence trace.

nodes.title: Polynomial coding and evaluation
nodes.statement: ∀b c x ell. ∃z. Horner(b,c,x,ell,z).
nodes.why: Seven original-kernel theorems independently close beta-coded natural Horner evaluation, including existence, uniqueness, the empty case, and successor decomposition. Arbitrary presented rings and formal differentiation remain separate downstream work.

nodes.title: Integer matrices and lattices
nodes.statement: ∀M r c. IntMatrix(M,r,c) → ∃t. t checks every requested finite entry, product, and determinant.
nodes.why: Alpha v25 independently constructs one complete beta-coded family of every genuine signed first-row cofactor minor, arbitrary parity-correct signed alternating cofactor folds, and a simultaneous actual-first-row/family/fold witness. Together with historical arbitrary signed products and signed determinants through dimension four, this yields 79 checked matrix components; unrestricted recursive determinant dimensions, rank, and lattices remain unproved.

nodes.title: Modular inverse
nodes.statement: ∀a m. m>1 ∧ Coprime(a,m) → ∃b<m. Mod(a*b,1,m).
nodes.why: A modular inverse is extracted from witnessed Bézout coefficients.

nodes.title: Strong induction and descent
nodes.statement: For each HA formula P: (∀n. (∀k<n.P(k))→P(n)) → ∀n.P(n).
nodes.why: Well-founded descent is derived from ordinary first-order induction.

nodes.title: Finite witnessed choice
nodes.statement: ∀ell. (∀i<ell.∃x.R(i,x)) → ∃s. Seq(s,ell) ∧ ∀i<ell.R(i,At(s,i)).
nodes.why: Induction concatenates only finitely many witnesses, not countable choice.

nodes.title: Existing quadratic reciprocity proof root
nodes.statement: ∀ distinct odd primes p,q. ∃a b. QuadBit(p,q,a) ∧ QuadBit(q,p,b) ∧ Mod(a+b,((p-1)/2)*((q-1)/2),2).

nodes.title: Existing Bertrand postulate proof root
nodes.statement: ∀n>1. ∃p. Prime(p) ∧ n<p<2*n.
nodes.why: The exact strict Bertrand theorem and its entire 544-theorem dependency graph now have unchanged-kernel and independent compiled-Lean proof evidence, including a separately accepted 201,285-node ordinary empty-context root certificate; Alpha v19 preserves checked use without inventing dependencies on the separately closed prime-valuation wrappers.

nodes.title: Existing quadratic supplementary laws
nodes.statement: ∀ odd primes p. ∃a b. QuadBit(p-1,p,a) ∧ Mod(a,(p-1)/2,2) ∧ QuadBit(2,p,b) ∧ Mod(b,(p²-1)/8,2).

nodes.title: Existing Kummer binomial carry theorem
nodes.statement: ∀p a b C v. Prime(p) ∧ Binom(a+b,a,C) ∧ PowerValuation(p,C,v) → CarryCount(p,[a,b],v).
nodes.why: Both exact immutable Alpha-v14 Kummer endpoints now have independently kernel-accepted ordinary empty-context proofs and a compiled-Lean-verified 280-theorem proof graph plus one synthetic conjunction; the exact carry theorem preserves its explicitly supplied coefficient and valuation hypotheses.

nodes.title: Existing full all-natural two-square classification
nodes.statement: ∀n. (∃x y.Rep2(n,x,y)) ↔ n=0 ∨ (n≠0 ∧ ∀q e. Prime(q) ∧ Mod(q,3,4) ∧ PowerValuation(q,n,e) → ∃h.e=2*h).

nodes.title: Existing unconditional Lagrange four-square theorem
nodes.statement: ∀n. ∃a b c d. Rep4(n,a,b,c,d).
nodes.why: The exact unconditional Alpha-v13 Lagrange root and its 390-theorem constructive descent now have independent unchanged-kernel and compiled-Lean evidence; the construction still predates and does not require either the all-natural two-square classification or unbuilt general matrices.

nodes.title: Existing multidigit Lucas theorem
nodes.statement: ∀p n k C. Prime(p) ∧ Binom(n,k,C) → ∃N K u. Digits(n,p,N) ∧ Digits(k,p,K) ∧ u=∏i Binom(Ni,Ki) ∧ Mod(C,u,p).

nodes.title: Existing primitive Pythagorean forward constructor
nodes.statement: ∀m>k>0. Coprime(m,k) ∧ m,k of opposite parity → ∃a b c. a=m²-k² ∧ b=2*m*k ∧ c=m²+k² ∧ PrimitiveTriple(a,b,c).

nodes.title: Division with unique quotient and remainder
nodes.statement: ∀n d>0. ∃q r. DivRem(n,d,q,r) ∧ ∀u v. DivRem(n,d,u,v)→u=q ∧ v=r.
nodes.why: Expose existing division as a uniquely witnessed reusable foundation, not a newly missing theorem.

nodes.title: Bézout identity and canonical gcd
nodes.statement: ∀a b. a+b>0 → ∃g u v. Gcd(a,b,g) ∧ u*a+v*b=g ∧ ∀h.Gcd(a,b,h)→h=g.
nodes.why: Package existing gcd and signed Bézout machinery into one canonical interface.

nodes.title: Euclid's coprime-product lemma
nodes.statement: ∀a b c. Coprime(a,b) ∧ Dvd(a,b*c) → ∃q.c=a*q.
nodes.why: Isolate the existing constructive divisibility cancellation foundation.

nodes.title: Existence of prime factorization
nodes.statement: ∀n>0. ∃s. Factorization(n,s).
nodes.why: Index already available prime-divisor descent as a finite factorization witness.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of prime factorization
nodes.statement: ∀n s t. Factorization(n,s) ∧ Factorization(n,t) → ∃w.Permutation(s,t,w).
nodes.why: Expose existing prime-factor uniqueness without claiming it is a novel open theorem.

nodes.title: Euler's totient product formula
nodes.statement: ∀n>0. ∃s t. Factorization(n,s) ∧ Phi(n,t) ∧ t=∏ over DISTINCT PRIME p∣n of p^(Val(p,n)-1)*(p-1).
nodes.why: Compute the finite multiplicative totient formula with witnessed prime factors.

nodes.title: Möbius inversion on divisors
nodes.statement: ∀N f g. ArithmeticTable(N,f) ∧ ArithmeticTable(N,g) ∧ (∀m.0<m≤N → g(m)=∑_{d∣m}f(d)) → ∃h. ∀n.0<n≤N → h(n)=∑_{d∣n}Mobius(d)*g(n/d) ∧ h(n)=f(n).
nodes.why: Require the divisor-sum hypothesis at EVERY POSITIVE input; zero has infinitely many divisors and is outside the finite tables.

nodes.title: Jordan totient multiplicativity
nodes.statement: ∀k a b. k>0 ∧ a>0 ∧ b>0 ∧ Coprime(a,b) → ∃u v w. Jordan(k,a,u) ∧ Jordan(k,b,v) ∧ Jordan(k,a*b,w) ∧ w=u*v.
nodes.why: Prove finite tuple-count multiplicativity with positive rank and positive modulus.

nodes.title: Finite signed Dirichlet-convolution algebra
nodes.statement: ∀N>0 ∀f g h. ArithmeticTable(N,f) ∧ ArithmeticTable(N,g) ∧ ArithmeticTable(N,h) → ∃w. w witnesses finite associativity, commutativity, delta identity, and inversion exactly when f(1)=1 or f(1)=-1.
nodes.why: Require N>0 so f(1) exists, quantify only finite signed table codes, and retain the exact unit-at-one inverse criterion.

nodes.title: Squarefree kernels and perfect-power classification
nodes.statement: ∀n>0. ∃r s w. Squarefree(r) ∧ n=r*s² ∧ PowerProfile(n,w) ∧ ∀u v.Squarefree(u) ∧ n=u*v²→u=r ∧ v=s.
nodes.why: Use valuations only at PRIME divisors and positive perfect-power exponents.

nodes.title: Generalized Chinese remainder theorem
nodes.statement: ∀data. CRTCompatible(data) → ∃x M. CRTSolution(data,x,M) ∧ ∀y.CRTSolution(data,y,M)→y=x.
nodes.why: Alpha v25 proves exact pairwise compatibility necessity, arbitrary non-coprime and zero-modulus finite CRT solution folding under a witnessed predecessor-LCM merge invariant, canonical positive-modulus uniqueness, unconditional gcd scaling, coprime-product gcd, and pairwise-compatible dominating-last canonical CRT. The universal implication from pairwise compatibility to every predecessor-LCM merge remains unproved.

evidence.available_scope: arbitrary non-coprime finite positive congruence systems under exact predecessor-LCM merge compatibility; zero-inclusive systems have witnessed solutions; pairwise-compatible dominating-last systems have canonical solutions
evidence.target_scope: every arbitrary pairwise-compatible potentially non-coprime finite modulus list with a canonical bounded simultaneous solution

nodes.title: Solvability of linear congruences
nodes.statement: ∀a b m g. m>0 ∧ Gcd(a,m,g) → ((∃x<m.Mod(a*x,b,m)) ↔ Dvd(g,b)).
nodes.why: The newly enrolled nine-row Alpha-v19 constructive tranche proves both directions of the exact gcd-divisibility criterion and constructs an actual strictly bounded residue at every nonzero modulus.

nodes.title: Coprime modular cancellation
nodes.statement: ∀a b c m. m>0 ∧ Coprime(a,m) ∧ Mod(a*b,a*c,m) → Mod(b,c,m).
nodes.why: The existing independently closed Stable theorem mod_eq_cancel_coprime proves the stronger exact nonzero-modulus form using a witnessed modular inverse.

evidence.statement_relation: exact nonzero-modulus theorem in conservative notation

nodes.title: Euler's theorem for units
nodes.statement: ∀a m t. m>1 ∧ Unit(a,m) ∧ Phi(m,t) → ∃w.Pow(a,t,w) ∧ Mod(w,1,m).
nodes.why: Certify Euler's theorem for explicitly invertible residues of every positive composite modulus.

nodes.title: Multiplicative order and minimal period
nodes.statement: ∀a m t. m>1 ∧ Unit(a,m) ∧ Phi(m,t) → ∃d.Order(a,(Z/mZ)*,d) ∧ Dvd(d,t).
nodes.why: Extract the actual least positive order and its witnessed totient divisibility.

nodes.title: Carmichael's universal exponent
nodes.statement: ∀m>1. ∃c.Carmichael(m,c) ∧ ∀a.Unit(a,m)→Mod(a^c,1,m).
nodes.why: Compute the minimal universal exponent from finite prime-power decomposition.

nodes.title: Primitive roots of odd prime powers
nodes.statement: ∀p k. Prime(p) ∧ p>2 ∧ k>0 → ∃g.PrimitiveRoot(g,p^k).
nodes.why: Exclude the exceptional noncyclic higher powers of two explicitly.

nodes.title: Classification of cyclic unit groups
nodes.statement: ∀m>1. (∃g.PrimitiveRoot(g,m)) ↔ ∃w.PrimitiveRootModulus(m,w).
nodes.why: State exactly the valid moduli 2, 4, odd prime powers, and twice odd prime powers.

nodes.title: Exponential congruence solvability
nodes.statement: ∀m e b t d u. (∃g.PrimitiveRoot(g,m)) ∧ Unit(b,m) ∧ Phi(m,t) ∧ Gcd(e,t,d) ∧ t=d*u → ((∃x.Unit(x,m) ∧ Mod(x^e,b,m)) ↔ Mod(b^u,1,m)).
nodes.why: Restrict the exact power-congruence criterion to cyclic unit groups.

nodes.title: Simultaneous polynomial congruences
nodes.statement: ∀data f. data lists pairwise coprime positive moduli and ACTUAL witnessed local roots of f → ∃x M.CRTSolution(data,x,M) ∧ ∀(a,m)∈data.Mod(f(x),0,m).
nodes.why: Glue provided local roots without falsely claiming roots exist at arbitrary moduli.

nodes.title: Euclid's infinitude of primes
nodes.statement: ∀B. ∃p.Prime(p) ∧ p>B.
nodes.why: Reindex the already available constructive finite-product proof, not a missing result.

nodes.title: Effective nth-prime upper bound
nodes.statement: ∀k>0. ∃s p.PrimeList(s,k) ∧ At(s,k-1,p) ∧ p<2^(2^k).
nodes.why: Give an explicitly finite doubly exponential search bound for the kth prime.

nodes.title: Prime divisors in binomial windows
nodes.statement: ∀n>1. ∃p z.Prime(p) ∧ n<p<2*n ∧ Binom(2*n,n,z) ∧ Val(p,z,1).
nodes.why: Seven independently checked original-kernel proofs derive a strict Bertrand-window prime dividing the central binomial coefficient with exact valuation one.

nodes.title: Iterated Bertrand prime chains
nodes.statement: ∀n>1 ∀k. ∃s.Seq(s,k+1) ∧ At(s,0,n) ∧ ∀i<k.Prime(At(s,i+1)) ∧ At(s,i)<At(s,i+1)<2*At(s,i).
nodes.why: Six independently checked original-kernel proofs use ordinary induction and exact beta-prefix extension to construct every finite strict Bertrand-prime chain.

nodes.title: Infinitely many primes three modulo four
nodes.statement: ∀B. ∃p.Prime(p) ∧ p>B ∧ Mod(p,3,4).
nodes.why: Eighteen independently checked Alpha-v23 proofs constructively decide the exact 3-mod-4 prime-divisor relation, perform actual bounded beta-coded factor search, apply the two-square obstruction, and use the subtraction-free Euclid number 4*(c-1)+3 to produce a genuine prime above every supplied bound.

nodes.title: Infinitely many primes one modulo four
nodes.statement: ∀B. ∃p.Prime(p) ∧ p>B ∧ Mod(p,1,4).
nodes.why: The independently checked ten-theorem Alpha-v19 proof takes a prime divisor of the constructive Euclid norm (2*c)^2+1 for a bounded common multiple c, excludes every prime below the bound and every 3-mod-4 prime using the existing two-square norm obstruction, and returns an explicit 1-mod-4 prime witness; it does not depend on the independently closed Alpha-v23 3-mod-4 infinitude theorem.

nodes.title: Effective Chebyshev prime bounds
nodes.statement: ∀x ell k. x≥2 ∧ BitLen(x,ell) ∧ PrimeCount(x,k) → x≤8*k*ell ∧ k*ell≤8*x.
nodes.why: Use entirely finite integer inequalities with explicit safe constants.

nodes.title: Bang–Zsigmondy primitive prime-divisor theorem
nodes.statement: ∀a>b>0 ∀n>1. Coprime(a,b) ∧ ¬((n=2 ∧ ∃j.a+b=2^j) ∨ (a=2 ∧ b=1 ∧ n=6)) → ∃p.Prime(p) ∧ Dvd(p,a^n-b^n) ∧ ∀k.0<k<n→¬Dvd(p,a^k-b^k).
nodes.why: State both exact exceptional families: exponent two with power-of-two sum, and (2,1,6).

nodes.title: Elementary arithmetized prime number theorem
nodes.statement: ∀k>0. ∃N. ∀n≥N. ∃ell u s w t. s>0 ∧ PrimeCount(n,t) ∧ LogBracket(n,ell/s,u/s,w) ∧ k*|t*ell-n*s|≤n*s ∧ k*|t*u-n*s|≤n*s.
nodes.why: Encode PNT entirely using finite rational logarithm brackets, explicit threshold witnesses, and signed integer error inequalities.

nodes.title: Dirichlet prime witnesses in coprime progressions
nodes.statement: ∀a q B. q>0 ∧ Coprime(a,q) → ∃p.Prime(p) ∧ p>B ∧ Mod(p,a,q).
nodes.why: Pose the full positive-modulus strict-HA progression-prime witness goal, including q=1, without analytic or search oracles.

nodes.title: Pascal recurrence and coefficient totality
nodes.statement: ∀n k. ∃z.Binom(n,k,z) ∧ (0<k≤n → z=Binom(n-1,k-1)+Binom(n-1,k)).
nodes.why: The exact choose_exists, choose_functional, and witnessed Pascal successor-cell recurrence are all independently kernel checked and Alpha-closed through the complete Lucas bundle.

nodes.title: Legendre's factorial valuation formula
nodes.statement: ∀p n e s. Prime(p) ∧ FactorialValuation(p,n,e) ∧ LegendreSum(p,n,s) → e=s.
nodes.why: The exact Alpha-closed theorem prime_factorial_valuation_eq_legendre_sum compares explicitly supplied factorial-valuation and witnessed finite quotient-sum inputs; its checked proof does not require the separately closed prime-power-valuation wrappers.

evidence.statement_relation: exact supplied factorial-valuation and Legendre-sum equality

nodes.title: Closed multidigit Lucas digit-product theorem
nodes.statement: ∀p n k C. Prime(p) ∧ Binom(n,k,C) → ∃N K u.Digits(n,p,N) ∧ Digits(k,p,K) ∧ u=∏i Binom(Ni,Ki) ∧ Mod(C,u,p).
nodes.why: The exact complete lucas_theorem root and all 213 actual constructive proof bodies are now independently kernel-checked and admitted without assuming a Kummer theorem.

nodes.title: Closed Kummer binomial carry valuation
nodes.statement: ∀p a b C v. Prime(p) ∧ Binom(a+b,a,C) ∧ PowerValuation(p,C,v) → CarryCount(p,[a,b],v).
nodes.why: The exact Kummer carry-count root is independently checked with its explicitly supplied binomial coefficient and valuation; the separately checked carry-free divisibility equivalence is a second genuine endpoint, not a silently strengthened hypothesis-free theorem.

nodes.title: Multinomial carry valuation
nodes.statement: ∀p n parts z. Prime(p) ∧ Multinom(n,parts,z) → ∃e.Val(p,z,e) ∧ CarryCount(p,parts,e).
nodes.why: Extend the existing binomial carry theorem to any finite witnessed summand list.

nodes.title: Lifting the exponent for odd primes
nodes.statement: ∀p x y n a b. Prime(p) ∧ p>2 ∧ x>y>0 ∧ n>0 ∧ Dvd(p,x-y) ∧ ¬Dvd(p,x*y) ∧ Val(p,x-y,a) ∧ Val(p,n,b) → Val(p,x^n-y^n,a+b).
nodes.why: Require odd PRIME p, positive nonzero difference, positive exponent, and unit inputs.

nodes.title: Wolstenholme's binomial congruence
nodes.statement: ∀p z. Prime(p) ∧ p≥5 ∧ Binom(2*p-1,p-1,z) → Mod(z,1,p^3).
nodes.why: Use the exact valid prime threshold p≥5 and a finite p-cubed congruence.

nodes.title: Jacobsthal's binomial congruence
nodes.statement: ∀p n k u v e. Prime(p) ∧ p≥5 ∧ 0<k<n ∧ Binom(p*n,p*k,u) ∧ Binom(n,k,v) ∧ Val(p,n*k*(n-k),e) → Mod(u,v,p^(3+e)).
nodes.why: State a valid LOWER divisibility bound, not an exact valuation, and exclude zero-valuation endpoints.

nodes.title: Prime-power Lucas unit decomposition
nodes.statement: ∀p n k q. Prime(p) ∧ k≤n ∧ q>0 → ∃z e u.Binom(n,k,z) ∧ Val(p,z,e) ∧ ¬Dvd(p,u) ∧ Mod(z,p^e*u,p^q) with a witnessed digit-factorial unit trace.
nodes.why: Keep p PRIME, k≤n so the coefficient is nonzero, and positive finite precision.

nodes.title: Complete p-adic multinomial congruence
nodes.statement: ∀p n parts q z. Prime(p) ∧ q>0 ∧ Multinom(n,parts,z) → ∃e u.CarryCount(p,parts,e) ∧ Val(p,z,e) ∧ ¬Dvd(p,u) ∧ Mod(z,p^e*u,p^q).
nodes.why: Combine prime-base carries and prime-power unit arithmetic at explicit positive finite precision.

nodes.title: Euler's quadratic criterion
nodes.statement: ∀p a h A. Prime(p) ∧ p=2*h+1 ∧ ¬Dvd(p,a) ∧ Pow(a,h,A) → (((∃x.Mod(x²,a,p)) ↔ Mod(A,1,p)) ∧ (¬(∃x.Mod(x²,a,p)) ↔ Mod(A,p-1,p))).
nodes.why: The Alpha-closed theorem arbitrary_euler_criterion_complete provides both residue and nonresidue equivalences for an odd prime, a nondivisible input, and the explicitly supplied finite power witness.

evidence.statement_relation: exact witnessed-power residue and nonresidue theorem in conservative notation

nodes.title: Gauss's quadratic-residue lemma
nodes.statement: ∀p h a b c. Prime(p) ∧ p=2*h+1 ∧ ¬Dvd(p,a) ∧ b,c code [1,…,h] → ∃e. e counts the witnessed Gauss reflections ∧ (((∃x.Mod(x²,a,p)) ↔ ∃j.e=2*j) ∧ (¬(∃x.Mod(x²,a,p)) ↔ ∃j.e=2*j+1)).
nodes.why: The Alpha-closed theorem arbitrary_gauss_lemma_complete constructs the reflection count from the supplied beta-coded half-range and proves both residue/even and nonresidue/odd equivalences.

nodes.title: Closed quadratic reciprocity over odd primes
nodes.statement: ∀ distinct odd primes p,q. ∃a b.QuadBit(p,q,a) ∧ QuadBit(q,p,b) ∧ Mod(a+b,((p-1)/2)*((q-1)/2),2).

nodes.title: Closed supplementary laws for minus one and two
nodes.statement: ∀p. Prime(p) ∧ p>2 → ∃a b.QuadBit(p-1,p,a) ∧ Mod(a,(p-1)/2,2) ∧ QuadBit(2,p,b) ∧ Mod(b,(p²-1)/8,2).

nodes.title: Jacobi-symbol reciprocity
nodes.statement: ∀ positive odd a,b ∀s t. Coprime(a,b) ∧ JacobiBit(a,b,s) ∧ JacobiBit(b,a,t) → Mod(s+t,((a-1)/2)*((b-1)/2),2).
nodes.why: Explicitly quantify both Jacobi sign witnesses and extend prime reciprocity to odd coprime composites.

nodes.title: Constructive Hilbert symbol at odd primes
nodes.statement: ∀ nonzero rational codes a,b ∀p. Prime(p) ∧ p>2 → ∃s<2.HilbertBit(a,b,p,s).

nodes.title: Cubic reciprocity in Eisenstein integers
nodes.statement: ∀pi rho s. Primary(pi,Eisenstein) ∧ Primary(rho,Eisenstein) ∧ RingPrime(pi,Eisenstein) ∧ RingPrime(rho,Eisenstein) ∧ pi,rho coprime → (PowerSymbol(pi,rho,3,s) ↔ PowerSymbol(rho,pi,3,s)).

nodes.title: Quartic reciprocity in Gaussian integers
nodes.statement: ∀ coprime primary Gaussian primes pi,rho ∀s t. PowerSymbol(pi,rho,4,s) ∧ PowerSymbol(rho,pi,4,t) → Mod(s-t,2*((Norm(pi)-1)/4)*((Norm(rho)-1)/4),4).

nodes.title: Hilbert reciprocity over rational places
nodes.statement: ∀ nonzero rational codes a,b. ∃w.HilbertProduct(a,b,w) ∧ the sum of all real-place, dyadic, numerator-prime, and denominator-prime local bits in w is even.
nodes.why: Include the real place, p=2, and EVERY prime dividing a numerator or denominator.

nodes.title: Prime-exponent cyclotomic power reciprocity
nodes.statement: ∀ell a b. Prime(ell) ∧ ell>2 ∧ a,b coprime admissible primary elements of the ellth cyclotomic integer ring → ∃w.PowerReciprocity(ell,a,b,w).
nodes.why: The exponent ell is prime, whereas the cyclotomic field degree is ell−1; all local corrections are mandatory.

nodes.title: Cauchy–Davenport sumset bound
nodes.statement: ∀p A B k l S m. Prime(p) ∧ FiniteSet(A,Fp,k) ∧ FiniteSet(B,Fp,l) ∧ k,l>0 ∧ SetSum(A,B,Fp,S) ∧ FiniteSet(S,Fp,m) → m≥min(p,k+l-1).
nodes.why: Prove the exact finite PRIME-field sumset bound with witnessed set cardinalities.

nodes.title: Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv zero-sum theorem
nodes.statement: ∀n>0 ∀s. Seq(s,2*n-1) → ∃w.ZeroSubsequence(s,n,Z/nZ,w).
